§YChaos Meter§!
The global Chaos Meter shortens event timing, unlocks stronger escalation, and increases eligible cluster pressure as its tier rises.

§YDeaths System§!
Military casualties and state-linked civilian deaths from war, disasters, disease, famine, forced displacement, camps, and unconventional weapons enter one shared ledger. Civilian entries remove real state population, and each source can convert its recorded toll into chaos.

§YAir Cleanliness§!
Air Cleanliness tracks atmospheric contamination from chemical hazards, outbreaks, fallout, smoke, ash, and aerosols. Thresholds at 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% accelerate outbreaks, worsen Air Winter, activate the Air Cleanliness Treaty, and can enable the Fallout consequence. Its Chaos Meter tab shows recovery and a permanent source ledger.

§YFamine Mechanics§!
Food shortages become a crisis when war, disasters, or disrupted supplies leave people without enough to eat. Hunger can kill civilians and drive survivors from affected regions. Relief supplies, restored transport, imports, and evacuation can protect your population and help the country recover.

§YMigration Mechanics§!
Migration affects your country when people flee war, persecution, hunger, or disasters, or when you receive those fleeing elsewhere. Flight reduces the population of affected regions, while arrivals can overwhelm local support. Border policies, safe routes, relief, settlement, and return decisions shape where people can live and whether they survive the journey.

§YCamp System Mechanics§!
Camps become relevant where your government uses detention or forced labor, including in occupied territory. Camps can cause civilian deaths and suffering, while exposed abuses can bring condemnation against those responsible. Reform and dismantlement decisions let you curb abuses or close the camps.
